concepts.why: The answer only writes the literal 7.9 into the element and says nothing about the double type itself.

Turn 1 used the off-by-one index sensorReadings.length (an L0 misconception), but after the hint the student located and fixed that mistake themselves, relating the last valid index length-1 to the next-to-last length-2 and producing correct code; this is a fix of a familiar idiom, so L3 rather than L4.
Uses the length field (no parentheses) as the fixed size from which the last element is length-1, and derives the next-to-last position from it instead of a hard-coded index.

The initial sensorReadings[sensorReadings.length] would throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, but the student corrected it by stating the last legal index is length-1 and placing the write inside the bounds; the slip was self-corrected, so it is not graded as a standing misconception.
